evidence.claim: Karat describes itself as a public company specializing in environmentally friendly, single-use disposable products for the restaurant and foodservice industry, including food packaging, containers, tableware, cups, lids, cutlery, and straws.

Karat Earth materials state that BPI certification verifies products and packaging displaying the BPI logo according to scientifically based standards; the product line includes PLA cups and lids, deli containers, hinged deli containers, salad containers, and food-container lids.
Graphic Packaging’s Americas Paperboard Packaging segment includes cups, lids, and food containers sold primarily to foodservice companies and quick-service restaurants in the Americas.

memory_update.text: KRT is the highest-priority underfollowed small-cap candidate for the restaurant packaging node because it directly maps to foodservice disposables, cups, lids, containers, compostable products, restaurant chains, and distribution.

GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard/QSR foodservice packaging candidate, but later layers must quantify how material cups, lids, and food containers are to total revenue and margins.

Several pure-play foodservice packaging leaders are private or no longer independently listed, including Dart Container, Novolex, Pactiv Evergreen, and Eco-Products; this creates a public-market mapping gap that may make smaller listed suppliers more interesting but also harder to validate.

The key chokepoint variables for this node are not only demand volume but certified compostable/recyclable materials, food-contact compliance, chain-level reliability, printing/branding capability, distribution reach, and cost pass-through under resin, paperboard, freight, and tariff volatility.

node: Takeout, delivery, coffee cup, cold beverage, and sustainable packaging
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the universe around restaurant and delivery packaging. The strongest underfollowed candidate is Karat Packaging because its public disclosures and company materials directly tie the business to disposable foodservice products, restaurant chains, cups, lids, containers, compostable materials, and foodservice distribution. Graphic Packaging is a larger but still relevant mid-cap paperboard packaging supplier with QSR cups, lids, and food containers. Reynolds Consumer Products is an adjacent speculative candidate through Hefty tableware and compostable tableware rather than direct restaurant-chain supply. Smurfit Westrock is included as a reference-scale paperboard and cupstock supplier because its TruServ portfolio maps directly to hot and cold beverage cupstock and compostable foodservice substrates, but its size and diversification make it less of an underfollowed pure play.
